correctness.rationale: The finite premise was recomputed from all 8192 binary words of length 13, all binary shorter lengths 3-12, and all 1594323 ternary words of length 13 using exact multiplicity-array equality; the 12 ternary collisions were checked against the full explicit list of binary-pair relabelings. Independent direct-index enumeration and dynamic programming agreed in 516 further cases. Alphabet merging preserves deck equality by partitioning admissible position tuples according to original patterns. Given any q-ary collision using three jointly occurring symbols, map two differing symbols and a third symbol to three distinct ternary labels: a distinct ternary collision with three jointly present letters would contradict the exact finite lemma. All q-ary collisions therefore use precisely two letters, giving four disjoint edges per unordered pair and no larger classes. Counting maximum independent sets in this matching establishes both exact formulas. The same letter-projection argument rules out q-ary collisions for lengths 3-12. Machine counters are exact 16-bit integers with maximal count 165.

originality.rationale: The binary length-13 threshold and four binary doubletons are acknowledged as prior evidence, not novelty. The genuinely additional finite ternary rigidity and the resulting arbitrary-alphabet edge-classification and exact q-ary optimum are not implied by the previously known binary list without excluding three-symbol collisions. Primary 2022 gapped-deck and 2023 (g,k)-binomial complexity texts and indexed related work were compared at the level of observation map, source class, length and implication. An unindexed equivalent finite-alphabet census remains a stated residual risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or incompletely accessible literature could contain an equivalent full ternary n=13 census or a general rigidity theorem.

Some adjacent-channel research-index results were inspected only as abstracts/summaries, not complete source texts; they are treated as inapplicable based on demonstrably different observation definitions, not as blanket novelty clearance.

value.rationale: This is the complete first-collision equivalence-class partition, zero-error code-size optimum, and optimizer count for every finite alphabet q. It resolves whether additional source symbols create new ambiguities—a nontrivial issue not answered by binary collision classifications. The ternary finite cutoff is decisive for all q by an exact alphabet-aggregation reduction, giving directly usable q-ary reconstruction bounds for natural multi-symbol sequence channels; the statement is not an arbitrary narrow slice, mere relabeling, or unmotivated isolated table entry.
